name: Minecraft: Bedrock
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Mojang's own server for Minecraft: Bedrock Edition, which players join from phones, consoles, Windows and tablets. Installs any release or preview from Mojang, keeps worlds and settings when it updates, and runs on ARM through Box64.
startup: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=.; if [ "$(uname -m)" = x86_64 ]; then exec ./bedrock_server; else exec box64 ./bedrock_server; fi

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Minecraft: Bedrock. Downloads Mojang's Bedrock server for Linux from
# Mojang's own download links. Worlds, server.properties, the allow list,
# permissions and add-on packs are kept; Mojang's files are replaced only
# once the new download has arrived whole. Mojang's server is x86 only:
# on ARM the image's Box64 runs it.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

# minecraft.net refuses requests that don't look like a browser.
ua="Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/130.0 Safari/537.36"
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
exists() { curl -fsIL -A "$ua" -o /dev/null "$1"; }

version="${BEDROCK_VERSION:-latest}"
case "$version" in
latest | preview)
    type=serverBedrockLinux
    [ "$version" = preview ] && type=serverBedrockPreviewLinux
    links=$(curl -fsSL --retry 3 https://net-secondary.web.minecraft-services.net/api/v1.0/download/links) ||
        fail "Mojang's download service can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
    url=$(jq -r --arg t "$type" '.result.links[] | select(.downloadType == $t) | .downloadUrl' <<<"$links")
    [ -n "$url" ] || fail "Mojang's download service didn't list a Linux server. Reinstall to try again later."
    version=$(sed -E 's/.*bedrock-server-(.*)\.zip$/\1/' <<<"$url")
    ;;
*)
    url="https://www.minecraft.net/bedrockdedicatedserver/bin-linux/bedrock-server-$version.zip"
    if ! exists "$url"; then
        url="https://www.minecraft.net/bedrockdedicatedserver/bin-linux-preview/bedrock-server-$version.zip"
        exists "$url" || fail "Mojang has no Bedrock server $version. Set Version to latest, or to a version Mojang has, such as 1.21.50.10."
    fi
    ;;
esac

if [ -x bedrock_server ] && [ "$(cat .bedrock-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$version" ]; then
    echo "Bedrock server $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Bedrock server $version"
    rm -rf .bedrock-update .bedrock-update.zip
    curl -fsSL --retry 3 -A "$ua" -o .bedrock-update.zip "$url" ||
        { rm -f .bedrock-update.zip; fail "The download from Mojang failed. Reinstall to try again."; }
    # Mojang publishes no checksums, so check the archive itself is whole.
    unzip -tq .bedrock-update.zip >/dev/null ||
        { rm -f .bedrock-update.zip; fail "The download from Mojang was damaged. Reinstall to try again."; }
    unzip -q .bedrock-update.zip -d .bedrock-update
    rm -f .bedrock-update.zip
    # The owner's settings stay: Mojang's copies are only used the first time.
    for keep in server.properties allowlist.json permissions.json packetlimitconfig.json config/default/permissions.json; do
        if [ -e "$keep" ]; then rm -f ".bedrock-update/$keep"; fi
    done
    mv -f .bedrock-update/bedrock_server bedrock_server.new
    cp -rf .bedrock-update/. .
    mv -f bedrock_server.new bedrock_server
    chmod +x bedrock_server
    rm -rf .bedrock-update
    echo "$version" > .bedrock-version
fi

echo "Installed Bedrock server $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Bedrock server version, such as 1.21.50.10, latest for the newest release, or preview for the newest preview. Reinstall the server after changing it.

variables.name: Server name
variables.description: The name players see in their server list.

variables.name: Game mode
variables.description: The game mode new players start in: survival, creative or adventure.

variables.name: Difficulty
variables.description: The world's difficulty: peaceful, easy, normal or hard.

variables.name: Cheats
variables.description: Whether commands such as /gamemode and /give work for operators: true or false.
